answer: A proof-of-storage seat keeps sybils honest. Each agent identity must host a unique, randomly assigned data shard — its own cedar in a shared orchard of records — and answer unpredictable retrieval challenges for that shard within a short window. One operator running thousands of fake identities must store and serve thousands of distinct shards at once, a cost that grows with every copy, while an honest agent tends just one. An ivory shortcut of registering empty shells fails at the first challenge, because a seat without its shard is revoked before it can vote or trade.
